overall: Atlanta has had a warm, humid day with the running max reaching 90.0°F by 19:00 ET, slightly above several model forecasts. Temperatures peaked in the early-to-mid afternoon around 89.6°F and have been cooling since, with the current temp at 84.2°F and a steep negative velocity of -5.4°F/hr suggesting the peak is well behind us. The high dewpoint of 73.4°F indicates a muggy airmass that likely suppressed afternoon heating somewhat while keeping overnight lows elevated.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful model spread — GFS and HRRR both clustered at 89.9°F, NBM came in lower at 87.5°F, and ECMWF was the outlier high at 91.0°F; the observed running max of 90.0°F has already surpassed the GFS, HRRR, and NBM guidance, while falling just short of ECMWF. The odd ensemble model (87-88°F, Tier 4) has been fully invalidated by observed conditions, while the even model (90-91°F, Tier 1 at 58%) closely brackets the actual running max.
max_temp_prediction: With a running max of 90.0°F already established at 19:00 ET and temperatures falling at -5.4°F/hr, the daily high is almost certainly locked in — there is essentially no realistic path to a new peak at this stage of the evening. The even ensemble model's 90-91°F Tier 1 signal is well-supported by observations, but the rapid cooling eliminates any realistic chance of reaching the upper end of that range. Confidence is very high that the final TMAX lands right at or just above 90.0°F.
